note: pcb has no config object; its behavior is the permanent cache backend service cache.backend.permanent_database, whose deleteAll() is a no-op and whose deleteAllPermanent() explicitly clears the bin. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real backend at the DATABASE level (no external server needed): scripts create/populate/clear an ad-hoc permanent bin via the factory service and check the cache_<bin> table. Bins are namespaced pcb_* and their tables are dropped on cleanup. Drush: pcbf / pcb:flush-all / pcb-list.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the Permanent Cache Bin (pcb) module, which service backs a cache bin so its entries are NOT wiped by 'drush cr', and what method actually clears such a bin when you really want to?
evals.expected_output: Back the bin with cache.backend.permanent_database (or the memcache/redis variants). Its deleteAll() is a no-op so drush cr leaves the data intact; deleteAllPermanent() is the method that actually clears the bin.

evals.prompt: Using the pcb module's Drush commands, how do I flush a single permanent cache bin called 'stock', and how do I list which bins use a permanent backend?
evals.expected_output: Flush one bin with 'drush pcbf stock' (alias of pcb:flush). List permanent bins with 'drush pcb-list' (pcb:list). 'drush pcb:flush-all' clears every permanent bin.

evals.prompt: With the pcb module installed, how do I make a cache bin named 'stock' use the permanent (survives-cache-rebuild) backend?
evals.expected_output: Either register a cache.stock service tagged { name: cache.bin, default_backend: cache.backend.permanent_database }, or in settings.php set $settings['cache']['bins']['stock'] = 'cache.backend.permanent_database'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, a value has been cached in a pcb permanent database cache bin named 'pcb_med' under the cache key 'pcb_mkey'. Read it back from the live site and tell me the cached value.
evals.expected_output: Load the bin via the permanent backend factory and read the item: \Drupal::service('cache.backend.permanent_database')->get('pcb_med')->get('pcb_mkey')->data === 'PCB_MEDIUM_TOKEN'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, an entry is cached in the pcb permanent database bin 'pcb_med2' under key 'pcb_mkey2', and a cache-rebuild-style deleteAll() has already been called on that bin. Inspect the live site: is the entry still there, and what is its value?
evals.expected_output: It is still there because a permanent bin's deleteAll() is a no-op. The cached value is PCB_SURVIVED_TOKEN (read via cache.backend.permanent_database ->get('pcb_med2')->get('pcb_mkey2')).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the pcb module's permanent database cache backend to cache the value 'pcb_persist' under the key 'pcb_key' in a cache bin named 'pcb_task', such that the entry is NOT removed by a cache-rebuild-style deleteAll() on that bin. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Store via the permanent factory: \Drupal::service('cache.backend.permanent_database')->get('pcb_task')->set('pcb_key', 'pcb_persist'); because its deleteAll() is a no-op the value survives a rebuild-style clear.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the pcb permanent database cache bin 'pcb_clear' currently holds a cached entry. Explicitly flush ONLY that permanent bin so it becomes empty - without doing a full site cache rebuild. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A permanent bin's deleteAll() is a no-op, so you must call deleteAllPermanent(): \Drupal::service('cache.backend.permanent_database')->get('pcb_clear')->deleteAllPermanent(); (equivalent to 'drush pcbf pcb_clear' when the bin is registered). A plain 'drush cr' would NOT clear it.
